title: Lina and Moss's Stone Secret
markdown:
The big oak made happy dancing shadows. Lina, smudged with grease, hummed as she walked. Beside her Moss the hedgehog waddled, nose twitching.

“Look!” He pointed to a stone. On it, a faint shape, like a leaf pressed inside.

Lina knelt. “It looks like a leaf. How is it in the stone?”

Moss thought. “Made a very, very long time ago? Maybe a leaf got stuck?”

“Or a giant bird dropped a leaf, and the stone grew around it!”

Moss giggled. “Or a huge beetle squished it!”

Auntie June, tending bright pink flowers, ambled over. “What marvels have you found?”

Lina traced the shape. “A perfect leaf, Auntie June, but how is it in the stone?”

Auntie June’s eyes twinkled. “That’s a fossil. Imagine an old plant falling into a river millions of years ago. Covered by soft mud and sand, tucked under a blanket. More mud piled on. The weight squeezed tighter and tighter, like a giant hug. Slowly the water helped turn the plant into stone, keeping its shape.”

Lina’s eyes lit. “Buried, squeezed, turned to stone!” A bubbly idea. “Can we make our own fossil?”

Auntie June chuckled. “A splendid idea. Soft squishy modeling clay. It won’t be millions of years old. It will show how a shape can be kept.”

Lina pressed clay smooth in a lid. Moss pressed his paw, a print.

“Now we cover it, like the old plants.” Dry soil over the print, then a little water. “Imagine this getting squeezed by more dirt, for a super, super long time.”

They looked. Moss’s paw was captured under soil, a shape kept safe.

“A model fossil!” Moss declared.

“Indeed,” Auntie June said softly. “Fossilization is nature’s way of keeping pictures from long ago in stone. Real ones take longer than an afternoon. Yours is a whisper of how the whisper gets made.”

Lina smiled at the ancient leaf in the real stone, then at the clay paw. Two kinds of keeping. She did not ask what else was hidden. She wrapped the lid so the print would not smear, and Moss, whose nose had found the first marvel, found a daisy to sniff, which is hedgehog for enough science for now.
